title: Payments slow right after release
executive_summary: Payment and order errors began about 11:28Z. Postgres showed the earliest anomaly: disk IO wait rose from ~2ms to ~107ms (onset 11:22Z), postgres p99 rose ~53x (onset 11:23Z), and a WAL/checkpoint stall was logged at 11:24Z. Statement timeouts on charges.insert and orders.update followed, and DB connection utilisation on both postgres and payment-service climbed to 80–96%. The payment-service 5.8.0 deployment occurred at 11:32Z, after error onset at 11:28Z, and its change is logging-only. Payment-service p99 latency and timeout rate were flat versus baseline, so the release does not explain the reported latency pattern. Recommended: fail over or migrate away from the degraded volume, and verify the storage volume with the infrastructure team.

hypotheses.description: Degraded block storage on postgres volume vol-0a3f causing slow WAL writes and checkpoints, which led to statement timeouts in payment-service and order-service and connection-pool saturation. Mechanism: Volume write latency rises (IO wait 2ms to ~107-160ms from 11:22Z). Checkpoints stall (453-497s) and WAL writes slow, so charges.insert and orders.update exceed the 2s statement timeout. Connections are held longer, DB connection utilisation rises to ~80-96%, and the apps see errors. The ordering fits: storage warning 11:21, IO wait 11:22, p99 DB 11:23, checkpoint 11:24, app errors 11:28.

probable_root_cause.label: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed)

root_cause_statement: MOST PROBABLE EXPLANATION (INFERENCE, not confirmed): infrastructure_degradation in postgres - Degraded block storage on postgres volume vol-0a3f causing slow WAL writes and checkpoints, which led to statement timeouts in payment-service and order-service and connection-pool saturation.
corrective_actions: Fail over postgres to a replica or migrate away from degraded volume vol-0a3f, after verifying the replica is healthy
Engage the cloud/infra team to check block-storage health and IOPS throttling for vol-0a3f
Do not roll back payment-service 5.8.0 on current evidence; roll back only if DB-side causes are ruled out
preventive_actions: Alert on postgres disk IO wait and WAL/checkpoint duration before they reach app-level timeouts
Review statement timeouts and retry policy for charges.insert and orders.update
Address report_rollup() long-running queries that compete for storage I/O
monitoring_recommendations: Monitor postgres disk_io_wait_ms and write latency per volume with alerting at about 20ms
Monitor checkpoint duration and WAL write latency
Track db_conn_util_pct on postgres and payment-service with alerting at 70%
Track payment-service error_rate and statement-timeout pattern counts
limitations: Correlation-based timing analysis; the storage cause is inferred, not directly observed
Payment p99 latency was flat, so the user-visible 'slowness' may reflect errors and retries rather than latency
Historical match (similarity 0.49) is only an analogy
[agent-reported gap] No cloud/host-level storage health data for vol-0a3f
[agent-reported gap] No pg wait-event or lock data
[agent-reported gap] No diff of the 5.8.0 code change beyond the summary
[agent-reported gap] No per-service connection pool breakdown
[agent-reported gap] Telemetry for the 60 minutes before T0 is only partially used; the baseline is clean
Confidence values are rule-based evidence-strength scores, not calibrated probabilities.
conclusion: The 5.8.0 release of payment-service is unlikely to be the cause. The onset of degradation precedes the deployment by several minutes and the release only added logging. The evidence points to degraded storage I/O on the postgres volume vol-0a3f (write latency and WAL/checkpoint stalls starting about 11:21–11:24Z), which caused statement timeouts and connection-pool pressure in payment-service and order-service. Final status is PROBABLE, not confirmed: the storage-level root cause is inferred from database-side telemetry and logs, and no infrastructure-level (cloud volume) evidence was collected.
